units.source_text: “他觉得还能活上十年二十年哪。

en.t: He thinks he can still live another ten or twenty years.

units.source_text: 可是他又常常说些让我担心的话。

en.t: But he also often says things that make me worry.

units.source_text: 他说什么，我这样子也活不了多久了。

en.t: He says things like, I probably do not have much longer like this.

units.source_text: 我要是死了，你怎么办哪，打算一个人在这房子里住下去吗？”

en.t: If I die, what will you do? Are you planning to go on living alone in this house?

units.source_text: 我眼前立刻浮现出父亲去世后，剩下母亲一个人孤单地住在这老旧而空荡荡的农舍里的情景。

en.t: At once I pictured the scene after my father died, with my mother left all alone in that old, empty farmhouse.

units.source_text: 死神把父亲从这个家拉走后，这个家还能存在下去吗？

en.t: After death had dragged my father away from this home, could the household still go on existing?
What would my elder brother do?

units.source_text: 牵挂着这些的我，还能离开这块故土，到东京去自由自在地生活吗？

en.t: With all these worries weighing on me, could I still leave this native place and live freely in Tokyo?

units.source_text: 面对着母亲，我偶然想起了先生的提醒：趁你父亲活着的时候，要把自己的那份遗产先分到手。

en.t: Facing my mother, I happened to remember Sensei's warning: while your father is still alive, get your own share of the inheritance settled first.

units.source_text: “没听说过谁老是说自己要死了，结果真的死了的，你就放心好了。

en.t: I have never heard of anyone who keeps saying he is going to die actually dying, so you can stop worrying.

units.source_text: 你爸总是念叨要死了、要死了的，其实不知还能活多少年哪。

en.t: Your father is always going on about dying, but who knows how many more years he may live.

units.source_text: 那种不爱说这话的健康的人，反倒危险呢。”

en.t: It is the healthy people who never say such things who are more in danger.

units.source_text: 我默不作声地听着母亲这套不知是从哪儿推论出来的迂腐论调。

en.t: I listened in silence to this stale argument of my mother's, not knowing what reasoning had led her to it.
